description.summary: whether, and how large, a surface is on screen

protocol.description:
This protocol tells a client whether one of its surfaces can currently be seen, so it can stop animating, decoding video or rendering at all while nothing it draws reaches the screen, and how large the compositor is showing it, so it can draw less detail while its window is a thumbnail in an overview.
Frame callbacks already stop for surfaces that are not drawn, but they say nothing about why, and nothing at all about a surface that is drawn as a small thumbnail. This protocol states both explicitly.
The information is advisory. A client must keep handling configure events and committing buffers whatever the reported state, and the compositor may show a surface it reported hidden at any moment, for example in a task switcher, before the next state event arrives.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_surface_visibility_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_surface_visibility_v1 objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Visibility objects created through it are unaffected.

request.name: get_surface_visibility
request.description:
Create an object reporting the visibility of surface. The compositor sends the current state and thumbnail scale, followed by done, right after the object is created.
surface should be the root surface of a toplevel or a layer surface. Any other surface, and a root surface that is not mapped, is reported hidden. Several objects may observe the same surface.

interface.name: crownos_surface_visibility_v1
interface.description:
Reports how one surface is shown. Each change is a group of state and thumbnail_scale events, carrying only the values that changed, ended by a done event; the client applies the group atomically on done.
Changes are coalesced: the compositor sends at most one group each time it updates its scene, which is at most once per output frame while anything animates. Values that animate, such as the scale of a window flying into an overview, are reported at the value they settle at rather than frame by frame.
If the surface is destroyed, the object becomes inert and should be destroyed.

entry.name: visible
entry.summary: at least part of the surface is drawn on some output

entry.name: occluded
entry.summary: the surface is on a visible workspace but fully covered

entry.name: hidden
entry.summary: the surface is not drawn anywhere

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the object. The compositor sends no further events for it.

event.name: state
event.description: Whether the surface is drawn. occluded means it would be drawn but something opaque covers all of it, such as a fullscreen window above it; hidden means it is not drawn at all, for example because its workspace is not shown, its window is unmapped or the session is locked.

event.name: thumbnail_scale

description.summary: the scale the surface is shown at changed

event.description: The factor the compositor draws the surface at, relative to its normal size: 1.0 when it is shown normally, below 1.0 while it is shown scaled down as a thumbnail, for example in an overview of every window. A client may lower its level of detail accordingly, but must keep drawing at its normal size; the compositor does the scaling.

event.name: done

description.summary: the end of a group of changes

event.description: Sent after a group of state and thumbnail_scale events, including the initial one, so the client sees them as one change.
